A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Morpher and the improved graph prompt. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, domain-transfer, synthetic zero-shot, ablation, and encoder-robustness results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds initialization-variance, model-size, pretraining-data-size, and expanded domain-transfer comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 retain the constrained cosine-based graph connections, graph and text prompts, frozen encoders, cross-modal projector, embedding normalization, contrastive loss, and similarity-based inference. The added initialization experiments concern AIO controls, not a revision of Morpher.

E1.justification: The graph, node, link-prediction, domain-transfer, synthetic ZERO-* and molecular prediction coverage is retained. The bace/tox21/hiv study moves from Section 5.7 to Appendix B.5. New scaling experiments use existing MUTAG data rather than introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Table 13 adds supervised training and original AIO to the domain-transfer comparison, which in v1 Table 3 contained fine-tuning, ImprovedAIO, and Morpher. GPF-plus and Gprompt remain in the full few-shot comparison, relocated to v3 Table 14.

E3.justification: New controlled experiments vary AIO initialization variance by 3, 5, and 10 times, GCN size across 1M/3M/10M parameters, and MUTAG pretraining fractions across 10%/30%/100%. These extend evaluation settings within retained tasks; the existing main experimental protocols are not substantively revised.

E4.justification: Appendices C.1 and C.3 add distinct investigations of whether high-variance initialization remedies AIO instability, whether GNN capacity improves Morpher, and how pretraining data volume affects performance. Existing component ablations and encoder/pretraining robustness studies remain. Table 15 redisplays existing language-encoder results rather than supplying new experimental outcomes.

E5.justification: V1 Section 5.1 explicitly identifies the few-shot results as averages over five runs. V3 removes that statement without supplying a replacement run count. This reduces statistical reporting detail but does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Existing full few-shot scores, transfer results, molecular results, and plotted findings are retained. V3 adds results in Tables 12-13 and 16-17; for example, MUTAG accuracy is 72.00%, 75.33%, and 78.67% across the new pretraining-fraction sweep. Its abbreviated main table also introduces different IMP summaries, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V3 deletes v1 Lemma 3.1, the elementary cross-entropy optimality result, and its Appendix A Lagrange-multiplier proof. The method's mathematical definitions and optimization equations otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 presents theoretical analysis of optimization restrictions as an explicit contribution; v3 recasts this as diagnosing and stabilizing graph-prompt training. The central claims about frozen-encoder multimodal prompting, weak supervision, and unseen-class generalization remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of initialization failure, scaling limitations, possible emergence thresholds, and the efficiency/expressiveness tradeoff of tuning frozen encoders. It also qualifies AIO's poor performance as setting-dependent and recommends domain-specific comparisons. Conversely, Section 5.1 removes v1's explicit exceptions to ImprovedAIO superiority, although those exceptions remain in Table 14.

D1.justification: V3 adds a direct code-repository link and explicit encoder/model-size information. However, it omits v1's weighted-F1 specification, 10-30-node ego-graph size, and construction of 200 positive plus 200 negative edge samples. Hardware, software environment, initialization instructions, and the approximate training/validation split are retained.

R1.justification: Although Section 6 is condensed, new appendix discussions substantially broaden research positioning around scaling laws, biomedical foundation models, graph distribution shifts, and graph generation. Added references include Kaplan et al., MedGTX, ProGen, and HyenaDNA; these changes extend beyond citation-format or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: V3 extensively condenses and rewrites the abstract, background, method explanations, and experimental narrative. It moves the molecular study into the appendices, brings limitations into the main text, reorganizes the appendices, and adds a substantial further-discussions section.

P2.justification: The document switches to two columns and substantially reorganizes displays. The introductory schematic moves to the appendix, the main few-shot table is abbreviated while its full version is retained, new diagnostic tables are added, and Appendix D enlarges existing plots without changing their underlying results.

improvement.justification: The initialization controls, fuller transfer comparisons, and limited scaling studies strengthen empirical scrutiny of the unchanged method. These provide a modest overall gain rather than a new level of validation. The benefit is tempered by lost run-count and sampling details and by Section 5.1's unqualified ImprovedAIO superiority statement despite the exceptions retained in Table 14.
